description: Solo team working on the 'Be An Earth System Trend Detective!' challenge — building a Flask dashboard that explores NASA temperature and precipitation trends.
summary: A Flask dashboard that picks a region (Lahore, Reykjavik, or Global) and a variable (temperature or precipitation) and draws the time series from real NASA data, fits a trend, and gives a plain-language verdict with slope per decade and p-value. Data: NASA POWER (monthly temperature and precipitation, 1981–2024, Lahore and Reykjavik) and NASA GISTEMP v4 (global land–ocean temperature anomaly, 1880–2025). Headline findings: global warming +0.212 °C/decade since 1981 (significant); Reykjavik +0.194 °C/decade (significant); Lahore is a dataset-disagreement story: NASA POWER shows no significant temperature trend (−0.061 °C/decade, p = 0.53), while the GISTEMP gridded cell containing Lahore warms significantly (+0.25 °C/decade, p ≈ 6×10⁻⁵ (Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall) over 1981–2024, with all eight neighbouring cells agreeing). The other headline findings stay as they are: global +0.212 °C/decade and Reykjavik +0.194 °C/decade, both significant; Lahore rainfall significantly up +0.153 mm/day/decade.
details: A Flask dashboard that picks a region (Lahore, Reykjavik, or Global) and a variable (temperature or precipitation) and draws the time series from real NASA data, fits a trend, and gives a plain-language verdict with slope per decade and p-value. Data: NASA POWER (monthly temperature and precipitation, 1981–2024, Lahore and Reykjavik) and NASA GISTEMP v4 (global land–ocean temperature anomaly, 1880–2025). Headline findings: global warming +0.212 °C/decade since 1981 (significant); Reykjavik +0.194 °C/decade (significant); Lahore is a dataset-disagreement story: NASA POWER shows no significant temperature trend (−0.061 °C/decade, p = 0.53), while the GISTEMP gridded cell containing Lahore warms significantly (+0.25 °C/decade, p ≈ 6×10⁻⁵ (Sen's slope, Mann-Kendall) over 1981–2024, with all eight neighbouring cells agreeing). Lahore rainfall is significantly up, +0.153 mm/day/decade (p = 0.016). Super-intelligence use: the starter for this project was built with Muse (Meta AI assistant), used for ideation, research, data analysis, coding and debugging, and writing and editing. No AI/ML is built into the app itself; it fits trends with ordinary least-squares regression on the NASA data.
